trigger: A hospital report, researcher report, or other information alleging the device failed to meet its specifications (including a security failure)
deadline: Record on receipt; review, evaluate, and investigate (no fixed day count in the regulation; internal target: complaint opened within 1 business day)
notify: Internal: eQMS complaint record
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - every product security event is screened as a possible complaint

trigger: Information that reasonably suggests the device may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury, or malfunctioned in a way likely to do so if it recurred (a compromised device that alters alarms can be such a malfunction)
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after any employee becomes aware (803.3 'become aware')
notify: FDA (electronic MDR)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - VP QA/RA decides and documents

trigger: An MDR reportable event needs remedial action to prevent an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to public health, or FDA asks in writing
deadline: No later than 5 work days after becoming aware
notify: FDA (electronic MDR)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if remedial action is needed

trigger: New information that was not known when the initial MDR was filed
deadline: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the information
notify: FDA (electronic MDR)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an MDR was filed

trigger: Company initiates a correction or removal (for example, a firmware fix or field action) to reduce a risk to health posed by the device or to remedy a violation that may present a risk to health
deadline: Within 10 working days of initiating the correction or removal (not required if already reported under Part 803 or exempt under 806.1(b))
notify: FDA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - unless the enforcement-discretion conditions below are all met

obligation: Record of a correction or removal not reported
trigger: A correction or removal is not reportable (for example a routine cybersecurity update for a controlled risk, or the enforcement-discretion path)
deadline: Keep the record with the justification; retain 2 years beyond the expected life of the device
notify: Internal: eQMS record reviewed by a designated person
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: customer communication (FDA enforcement discretion condition)
citation: FDA guidance, Postmarket Management of Cybersecurity in Medical Devices (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Vulnerability assessed as an uncontrolled risk to safety and essential performance, with no known serious adverse events or deaths
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after learning of the vulnerability: tell customers and users, give interim compensating controls, and have a remediation plan
notify: Hospital customers and user community; the ISAO (copy of the communication)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - guidance, not a regulation; meeting all conditions means FDA does not intend to enforce 806 reporting

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: fix distributed (FDA enforcement discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Same as above
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 60 days after learning of the vulnerability: fix, validate, and distribute the deployable fix
notify: Hospital customers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - guidance

obligation: ISAO participation and sharing (FDA enforcement discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), sections VII.B and IX (nonbinding)
trigger: Company communicates with customers about a vulnerability
deadline: Share customer communications with the ISAO when customers are notified; active ISAO membership is a condition of the enforcement-discretion path
notify: ISAO that shares medical device vulnerabilities
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - membership not yet active (POAM-004, due 2026-10-31)

trigger: Critical vulnerability that could cause uncontrolled risks in a cyber device or related system
deadline: Make updates and patches available out of cycle as soon as possible (no day count in the statute)
notify: Hospital customers (via the update service or field service)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for PM-2 (cleared after 524B took effect); PM-1 follows the postmarket guidance

trigger: A researcher or other party reports a vulnerability
deadline: Acknowledge within 3 business days; agree a public disclosure date
notify: Reporter; optionally CISA for coordinated public advisory
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company commitment (policy due 2026-10-31)

obligation: Business associate breach notice to hospitals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held in the device cloud (discovered on the first day known, or that by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, or other agent of the company other than the person committing it)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; include each affected individual's identity to the extent possible and other information the hospital needs for its notices
notify: Each affected hospital (covered entity) through the BAA contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - device cloud only

obligation: Security incident report under the BAA
trigger: Any security incident involving the device cloud of which the company becomes aware
deadline: As set in each BAA (many are shorter than 60 days); check the BAA terms register (POAM-016)
notify: Each affected hospital
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual timing varies by hospital

trigger: A law enforcement official states that notice would impede a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if the statement is oral and documented
notify: Hold hospital notices; document the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a hospital that holds personal information of Florida individuals (medical information with a name counts)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred; give the hospital all information it needs for its notices
notify: Each affected hospital (the covered entity under 501.171)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - shorter than the HIPAA 60-day limit, so it sets the clock

trigger: Hospital determines a breach occurred
deadline: Hospital's deadlines; the company supplies information promptly
notify: Individuals, HHS, media, Florida Department of Legal Affairs (by the hospital)
applies_at_this_tier: No - hospital duty; the company supports

obligation: State data breach notification (company's own personal information)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information the company holds for itself (for example employee records)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Only if company-owned personal information is affected; apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion is involved (POL-03 4.8)

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; the proposed criteria would cover manufacturers of Class II or III devices, so recheck when final

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no defense contracts

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
